method: tools/compare/cursePaletteTimingProbe.py (fresh direct mGBA, instruction stepping at BeginNormalPaletteFade CpuSet; no framebuffer read) on the two accepted Ghost scenarios and the two prep14/prep23 alternates
question: Is the row-26 palette-transfer scanline (prep23 P1) derivable from the body source timing or the activation frame the production queue knows?
verdict: NOT DERIVABLE: the same CurseGhost script position (first Step2 row, body row 26) on the same side samples REG_VCOUNT 17 + HBlank (scanline 18, HAUNTER->MAGIKARP) vs 9 (scanline 9, GENGAR->GOLEM): the transfer lands after the frame main loop CPU work that precedes the task (VBlank m4a sound mixing, battle controllers, text printers, palette fade), a CPU-cycle phase the production queue does not carry (it knows the activation frame index, not cycles). R1 (BG2 scroll one row early in 2/4 windows) is the same main-loop-vs-VBlank phase. The Ghost branch declines to the scene-off view (prep23 alternate residual at row 26: 135 / 15 px).
